title: Integral vanishing cycles: reconstruction and analytic applications
description: The reconstruction of marked vanishing cycles is now presented separately from the known topological classification and the analytic applications. The abstract specifies the recovered integral data, the two small Hodge eigenvalues and the complete low spectral tangent space for Hermitian–Yang–Mills flow. Established analytic statements are collected in an appendix, with their hypotheses verified on the constructed family.

title: Integral vanishing cycles: topology and marked recovery
description: Integral topology determines the primitive rank-six vanishing lattice, torsion-free quotient and symplectic normal form in the eight-node conifold family. The terminating period construction recovers coordinates in an independently constructed geometric marking and the associated monodromy matrices. The matrix is constant in the transported marking, so one reference-fibre recovery suffices.

title: Point defects and Hermitian–Yang–Mills flow on surfaces
description: For rank-two extensions with distinct equal-degree line factors and nonempty reduced point defects on a compact Kähler surface, every smooth initial metric with the fixed Hermitian–Einstein determinant has an explicit inverse-time inclusion-norm law. Actual metrics converge to a charge-one anti-self-dual profile at radius of order T⁻¹ᐟ², with matching leading inclusion half-height and half-energy radii. Arbitrary finite defects satisfy an O(T⁻¹) bound, strengthened to o(T⁻¹) when a defect is nonreduced; sharp profiles beyond the reduced distinct-factor class remain open.

title: Integral vanishing cycles from periods on conifold smoothings
description: Certified period jumps recover the marked integral vanishing-cycle homomorphism for an algebraically selected six-parameter conifold family, including saturation, quotient torsion and monodromy. The terminating construction produces a geometric symplectic marking and absolute observation-error bounds without a height prior. Relative Ricci-flat Hodge spectra and nonflat bundle dynamics apply on a possibly ineffective smaller neighbourhood of the same family; the full integral matrix is not numerically executed, and reconstruction of an arbitrary manifold is not asserted.

title: Hermitian–Yang–Mills dynamics and harmonic moduli near a conifold
description: A nonflat rank-four bundle family on Ricci-flat conifold smoothings admits relative asymptotics for all seven weak endomorphism modes, including changing kernels and independently separated rates. For an open spatial C¹ basin, actual Hermitian–Yang–Mills flow follows an exact finite invariant-graph trajectory with an initial phase and exponentially decaying C¹ error for all time. Harmonic metrics on every local stabilizer stratum determine a confined metric tangent cone; base and bundle scales vary independently, while each trajectory fixes its base and holomorphic bundle.

title: Relative Hodge spectra of multiscale conifold smoothings
description: Actual Ricci-flat metrics on an explicit eight-node Calabi–Yau conifold smoothing have exactly two small positive two-form eigenvalues throughout a six-dimensional period base, with no restriction on nonzero node ratios. A relative comparison of the full energy and harmonic mass identifies both eigenlines and a complementary spectral gap. Independently scaled Stenzel regions give logarithmic and iterated-logarithmic hierarchies on the same algebraic family.

title: All-time approximation of Hermitian–Yang–Mills flow on degenerating curves
description: Hermitian–Yang–Mills flow on a compact genus-three family admits an absolute approximation uniform for all time as four node parameters and two component-holonomy parameters tend independently to zero. Fixed holonomy generators and node identifications, uniformly bounded actual initial metrics and small finite initial data are retained, but no lower bound on the weakest decay rate is required. A global divergence representation and energy estimates control every relaxation time; the same family has complete relative spectral asymptotics and an example with h⁻¹, h⁻² and h⁻⁴ time scales.

title: Hermitian–Yang–Mills flow on degenerating Calabi–Yau threefolds of type K
description: A compact Enriques Calabi–Yau degeneration carries a nonflat rank-four Hermitian–Einstein bundle family whose five small endomorphism eigenvalues admit relative asymptotics through strict polystability. A constrained noncommuting matrix flow tracks actual Hermitian–Yang–Mills trajectories for prescribed product-induced Kähler metrics, including entry from non-tensor spatial data. Tracking holds on bounded logarithmic time intervals and for all time under a positive effective-rate bound; the spectrum also recovers projective cycle transport within the specified family.

title: Hermitian–Yang–Mills flow and gluing on degenerating curves
description: On compact degenerating curve families, noncommuting unitary gluing gives a finite matrix flow that approximates actual Hermitian–Yang–Mills trajectories, with relative control of every small eigenvalue and entry from an open spatial class. Independent node lengths and weak component holonomy are permitted in their stated families; all-time tracking requires a positive normalized rate. A Hodge-metric comparison and marked spectral observations recover projective gluing, and a separate finite class recovers unknown incidence and integral monodromy.

title: Effective Hermitian–Yang–Mills flow on nodal degenerations of curves
description: On trivial determinant-one bundles over compact nodal curve degenerations, actual noncommuting Hermitian–Yang–Mills metric flow follows a finite matrix graph flow on logarithmic time scales. Component areas supply the masses and each node supplies a coupling. For uniformly bounded initial metrics with prescribed local L² limits, the comparison gives global L² tracking on bounded rescaled time intervals and pointwise tracking away from the nodes after a fixed physical-time transient.

title: Small Hodge eigenvalues on nodal degenerations of threefolds
description: For nodal degenerations of compact threefolds with smooth Kähler total space and induced fibre metrics, exceptional periods and a quotient harmonic norm determine all leading small positive two-form eigenvalues. The small resolution must have vanishing first Betti number and second real cohomology generated by line-bundle classes. The small forms are coexact, primitive and of type (1,1), with a gap in the remaining positive spectra in degrees one and two.

title: Small eigenvalues on degenerating curves and the intersection form
description: For reduced degenerations of compact curves with smooth total space and metrics Hermitian near the central singularities, the complete small scalar spectrum is determined by the negative intersection matrix relative to component areas. The leading coefficients are 2π times its positive generalized eigenvalues, with inverse-logarithmic decay and a gap in the remaining spectrum. A direct proof allows arbitrary singularities of the reduced central curve and identifies the product coefficient through weighted spanning trees.

title: Atiyah–Floer cobordism bibliography revision
description: References to the mod-two Atiyah–Floer cobordism comparison now identify arXiv:2611.10002 in the integral comparison and normalization bibliographies. The mathematical statements and proofs are unchanged.

title: Calabi–Yau conifold spectra: metric comparison and spectral proof
description: Small positive Hodge eigenvalues in fixed polarized Ricci-flat conifold smoothings are determined by exceptional periods and global quotient harmonic norms. The revised proof separates the ordered spectral law on exact conic models from its transfer under pointwise metric comparison, and establishes that comparison for the prescribed family with finitely many nodes. The finite-cap compactness argument is explicit; the stronger differentiated estimate is reserved for the rank-one remainder. Supporting integral topology and tangent-sheaf calculations appear in appendices.

title: Integral topology and small eigenvalues in Calabi–Yau conifold transitions
description: Exceptional periods and global intersections determine the leading small two-form spectrum of Ricci-flat metrics in fixed polarized Calabi–Yau conifold smoothings. With a simply connected projective small resolution and first-order smoothing at every node along a fixed ray, exactly the lost divisor directions yield positive eigenvalues tending to zero. Their inverse-logarithmic coefficients use the harmonic norm after projection off all surviving cohomology. Four-node and eight-node toric families and the sixteen-node split quintic give explicit coefficients; the quintic also has calculated integral rings, attachments, specialization and monodromy. The four-node application uses the original-side family established in the Calabi–Yau smoothing programme.

title: Scalar scattering across separated Higgs scales
description: Scalar scattering in a smooth heterotic K3 family admits a uniform light-vector comparison as the Higgs scales separate. The complete leading Yang–Mills tree amplitude includes every internal vector and scalar mode, below the heavier Higgs masses and away from the light poles. Actual harmonic-state estimates and an exact contact–exchange cancellation also give a selected curvature coefficient with uniform inverse-square growth. Relative vector corrections, quadratic potential mixing with K3 metric deformations and universal graviton exchange are controlled separately; the complete next heterotic coefficient and finite-string-scale remainders remain open.

title: Clickable bibliography DOIs for heterotic K3 enhancement
description: The DOI references to the two companion geometric papers now open their archived versions directly. The printed text, mathematical results and physical approximations are unchanged.

title: Light vectors and scalar interactions near heterotic K3 gauge enhancement
description: Light-vector masses near gauge enhancement in an SO(32) heterotic K3 compactification admit relative geometric control even when the Higgs scales separate arbitrarily. The first tree vector correction includes the complete leading metric and two-form towers and preserves the unbroken gauge kernels. In the same bundle family, a compensated reduction identifies a leading neutral-scalar interaction with inverse-square growth at fixed positive deformation ratio. The vector estimate concerns a defined first-order system; the scalar statement extracts the tree large-volume coefficient before enhancement. Uniform finite-string-scale remainders remain open.

title: Canonical metrics on singular moduli of K3 bundles
description: Canonical singular Ricci-flat metrics on a class of compact K3 bundle moduli spaces admit quadratic approximation by their hyperkähler tangent cones in holomorphic coordinates. Twice-primitive Mukai vectors and a rank bound exclude non-locally-free sheaves and slope-graded factors. The harmonic L² metric equals the canonical metric in an ample determinant class, and its regular-locus completion recovers the original space. The comparison is uniform through stabilizer changes within each fixed chart, even though these moduli spaces have positive-dimensional singular strata and admit neither a symplectic resolution nor a global smoothing.

title: Integral attachments and wall correspondences for K3 bundle moduli
description: A compact six-chamber family of rank-three K3 bundle moduli admits an explicit integral calculation of its complements, boundary restrictions and adjacent wall actions. Four crossings are corrected Mukai flops and two are divisorial isomorphisms whose opposite divisor signs determine a reflection. Hilbert-square transport gives integral coordinates for the exceptional surfaces and determinant-normalized universal indices, including the boundary restriction modulo eight. The resulting cycles have exact periods and volumes in the established harmonic metric degeneration of this family.

title: Clarified limit arguments for compact K3 moduli
description: The compact K3 degeneration arguments now specify arbitrary-sequence convergence, uniform moving-fibre limits and successive rescalings under the stated quotient hypotheses. The revisions clarify the proofs and integral-cycle conventions while preserving the main conclusions.

title: Exceptional cycles and harmonic metrics in K3 bundle moduli
description: Compact K3 bundle-moduli fourfolds connect interacting exceptional planes to primitive integral classes, a boundary attachment modulo eight, and the actual harmonic metric. A moving projective line specializes with multiplicity one to the sum of two plane lines. Exact areas and volumes, ambient diameter estimates through separated scales, and complete rescaled limits describe the same cycles; the chamber metrics converge to the completed central harmonic metric.

title: Integral reconstruction and quantitative metric degeneration of K3 bundle moduli
description: A compact rank-seven K3 bundle-moduli eightfold realizes moving projective lines and a deepest Grassmannian fibre Gr(2,4), with both middle Schubert classes extending integrally and an explicit attachment modulo six. Exact harmonic periods, volumes and ambient diameter asymptotics accompany a general quantitative comparison theorem for compact K3 contractions without bubbling. Additive reconstruction retains cochains on all overlaps, monodromy and a marked complement ring.

title: Uniform asymptotic phase for Hermitian–Yang–Mills flow near a polystable bundle
description: Near a fixed locally free polystable bundle, confined Hermitian–Yang–Mills trajectories admit an exact finite-dimensional comparison flow selected through a continuously differentiable initial-phase map. Relative metric error decays exponentially at a rate controlled by the complementary elliptic gap, uniformly through changing stabilizers and arbitrarily separated positive finite scales. The construction retains the full convergent obstruction and arbitrary multiplicities, including noncommuting automorphisms and unbounded reconstructing gauges. An obstructed bicubic family supplies explicit noncommuting integrable examples; confinement and small initial normal displacement remain hypotheses.

title: Quantitative local models for Hermitian–Einstein metrics
description: Near a fixed locally free polystable bundle on a compact Kähler manifold, the full convergent deformation model gives uniform relative estimates for Hermitian–Einstein metrics, every small endomorphism eigenvalue, and harmonic quotient metrics on reduced smooth pieces. The estimates persist through changes of stabilizer and arbitrarily separated positive scales, with quadratic error in canonical harmonic coordinates and moving harmonic backgrounds. A stable rank-two bundle on a smooth bicubic Calabi–Yau threefold has essential cubic deformation equations; the comparison applies to the complete deformation family of three copies.

title: Quantitative metric wall crossing for K3 bundle moduli
description: Near polystable K3 bundles satisfying the stated stability hypotheses, harmonic moduli metrics admit a uniform comparison with quiver quotient metrics, even as stabilizers change and positive scales separate. A rank-five, two-parameter example realizes five walls, with local contraction profiles and intrinsic distance asymptotics. Under the stated quiver hypothesis, finite successive rescalings have complete limits whenever normalized parameters and balanced base representatives converge at each stage.

title: Metric wall crossing in rank-three K3 bundle moduli
description: Uniform comparison with hyperkähler quotient metrics describes local harmonic metric wall crossing in a rank-three K3 bundle moduli space. It yields collapse scales, complete rescaled limits modeled on cotangent bundles of Grassmannians and intrinsic distance asymptotics, including through changes of stabilizer.

title: Harmonic paths and honeycombs
description: Every full split boundary triple in the specified A₂ setting admits a harmonic norm path with finite labelled honeycomb support, in every finite rank. Uniqueness holds among paths with finite apartment presentations whose one-sided norm motions agree to first order at each join.

title: General acyclic cancellation and nonbalanced relaxation
description: Acyclic cancellation holds for surjective source differentials, arbitrary surviving tuples and unequal dimensions, with fixed charges and a sufficiently large least acyclic singular value. At fixed dimensions and total norm bounds, the estimates are uniform in arrow count, stabilizer and acyclic condition number. A separate finite-infimum theorem gives nonbalanced cohomology relaxation; balanced and Pauli cases are corollaries. Nonscalar static estimates accompany a sharp C² regularity example.

title: Conifold relations: companion arXiv references
description: Companion arXiv records are now cited in the bibliography. The revision preserves the original manuscript date and adds a separate version date. The PDF, sources and Zenodo archive are updated; the mathematical text and abstract are unchanged.

title: Mass increase and acyclic cancellation
description: Categorical phase flows for two-term quiver complexes can increase mass. An explicit example accompanies exponential acyclic cancellation for invertible differentials and uniform comparison with instantaneous cohomology in a specified stabilizer-changing mixed family.

title: Singular HYM metric growth: a general surface theorem
description: For rank-two bundles on compact Kähler surfaces with a saturated equal-slope line subsheaf and a singular torsion-free quotient, two bounded-remainder descriptions of Hermitian–Yang–Mills metric growth fail. The obstruction includes nonreduced singularities and repeated line factors, with a projective K3 example. The stationary curvature theorem retains its toric hypotheses.

title: Stability and Geometric Degeneration: a programme guide
description: A focused guide follows the programme from realizable chambers to small spectra, moduli metrics and geometric flows. It explains why relative accuracy matters, distinguishes changing stabilizers from singular graded sheaves, and presents the counterexample, reading routes and remaining questions alongside the scope of the established results.

title: Metrics, moduli and flow near stability walls
description: Three-step extension geometry connects actual Hermitian–Einstein metrics, local moduli metrics and initial-condition-sensitive Hermitian–Yang–Mills flow. A toric surface example shows why singular graded sheaves require a different metric asymptotic law.

title: Atiyah–Floer cobordism series: revised introductions and DOI references
description: Revised introductions trace the progression from comparison over 𝔽₂ to integral naturality with transported orientations, and then to identification and normalization of the usual cobordism maps. Companion references now include Zenodo DOIs. The original manuscript dates are preserved alongside separate version dates.

title: A focused Atiyah–Floer research guide and a seventh explorer move
description: A new research guide, nested under the topology guide, presents the Atiyah–Floer programme in five sections: the question of functoriality, the cobordism papers as a progression from parity to signs to conventions, the point-operations paper and its bubbling corrections, a table of what is proved and what remains open after Paper III, and the reading order with the hypotheses each theorem carries. The cobordism explorer gains a seventh move, which compares the two orientation systems of Paper III on an exact integral model.

title: Atiyah–Floer cobordism maps III: usual maps and integral normalization
description: The usual singular Hopf-link cobordism maps agree with the signed mixed-count comparison under the stated analytic, naturality, surgery and oriented-gluing inputs. Finite integer linear combinations of products of geometric counts realize sphere-positive normalization for every closed connected oriented three-manifold. Comparisons with prescribed relative-spin maps and the nonsingular cap convention remain open.

title: Uniform Hermitian–Einstein spectra with repeated stable factors
description: An independently balanced matrix model determines every small Hermitian–Einstein endomorphism eigenvalue for simple two-step extensions with repeated stable factors, with uniform relative accuracy at arbitrarily separated positive scales. A fixed rank-five geometric example exhibits the scale separation. Flow and higher-step questions remain open.

title: Toric tangent stability: complete census and geometric extensions
description: A complete exact eightfold census certifies 64 stable, 692 strictly semistable and 5,525 unstable cases, with every strictly semistable case a product. Further results give positive spanning without local freeness, a Bott-filtration obstruction and an eight-node Calabi–Yau transition.

title: When Walls Collide: find the missing wall
description: A new explorer follows one exact quartic example in open FJRW theory. Take two paths, find the correction that makes their operations agree, transport a lattice frame around an annulus, and compare full potentials with the period class that misses their difference. Four experiments and a threshold grid connect the calculations to the papers and their remaining geometric question.

title: At the Wall: how geometry loses rigidity
description: A new explorer links stability chambers, weighted extension graphs, small eigenvalues and metric response. Four experiments follow three vanishing scales, compare trees with cycles, and examine the two-factor flow across a stability wall, with the finite calculations and their geometric scope explained alongside.

title: Universal curve counting across Calabi–Yau transitions
description: A rational universal conifold-specialization formula is established and evaluated in a complete compact calculation. A compact counterexample rules out general integrality for scalar local-curve factors.

title: Research programmes within the guides
description: The research guides now set out the programmes inside each subject: what the papers establish, the theorem or construction still missing, and why it would matter. New sections cover Atiyah–Floer comparisons, open FJRW scattering, compact Higgs transitions, black-hole information, inverse moduli theory and evidence-based capital allocation, each labelled by how far the work has come.

title: Relative metric estimates near reducible Yang–Mills connections
description: Near a central Yang–Mills connection on a closed surface, a finite-dimensional model controls the quotient metric and every small gauge eigenvalue uniformly through changing stabilizers and arbitrarily separated scales. Green operators determine the leading metric correction; quaternionic reductions provide explicit curved comparisons.

title: Stability and Geometric Degeneration
description: Uniform small Hermitian–Einstein spectra and metric-response estimates connect realizable toric tangent stability chambers to actual Hermitian–Yang–Mills flow. Geometric and analytic reading routes set out the results and their hypotheses.

title: Small Dolbeault eigenvalues near stability walls
description: In the stated two-step extension setting, ranks and slope gaps determine the leading small Hermitian–Einstein endomorphism spectrum near intersecting stability walls, with uniform relative accuracy across independent positive gaps. A second-order two-factor expansion and toric examples exhibit finer asymptotics and arbitrarily many spectral scales.

title: Local stability chambers for toric tangent bundles
description: A family of toric projective bundles admits a complete tangent-stability classification and local chambers with arbitrarily many independent boundaries. Geometric criteria determine nearby stable polarizations in all 31 indecomposable semistable census cases.

title: The same law in a black hole and a stock market
description: An interactive essay: the Marchenko–Pastur law, written down in 1967 for neither, governs the noise in a correlation matrix and the radiation of an evaporating black hole.

title: One year per year
description: An interactive essay on alpha discovery when hypotheses are free and the evidence that judges them still arrives at the speed of the calendar.

title: Nobody did it
description: An interactive essay on deterrence when delegating decisions to machines produces acts with no author.

title: Why broken things make invariants
description: An interactive essay on how gauge theory and Floer theory build invariants from the ways their solutions break.

title: Who vouches for a machine?
description: An interactive essay on the trust layer machine commerce still lacks: a court, a ledger, an underwriter, and the prices that would feed them.

title: Two ways for a theory to fail
description: An interactive essay on geometric and informational singularities, from Norton’s dome to the island formula.

title: The balance point of a hexagon
description: An interactive essay on slope stability, Kähler–Einstein metrics, and six arrows that balance on average and still lean.

title: Nothing condenses alone
description: An interactive essay on Higgs transitions in compact Calabi–Yau threefolds, where gravity turns local symmetries into shared constraints.

title: A page for every paper
description: The collection now has individual abstract pages, citation downloads, and archive links, with verified PDF copies hosted here where available.

title: Mirror symmetry for conifold relations
description: For specified Batyrev mirror families, relations among exceptional curves and mirror vanishing three-spheres agree as integral lattices on nodal components meeting the construction near the maximally degenerate limit. The comparison determines codimension and characterizes smoothability; a smoothing yields a symplectic conifold transition on the mirror.
